title: Where the legacy code goes wrong, and how randolist fixes it
text: n.block_permute = 1 patient numbers shuffled within block. list cut nPat last block holds single patient, patient forms permutation group one. legacy code shuffles sample(x), single number x R’s sample(x) draws 1:x: block length 4 41 patients, patient 41 alone last block: Two patients receive randomisation number, one number missing list. new code keeps correct ID; every row legacy list:
code: set.seed(1) sample(41)[1:5]   # not "41": a permutation of 1:41 #> [1]  4 39  1 34 23 # first seed for which the legacy list has a duplicated ID has_dup <- function(s) {   set.seed(s)   anyDuplicated(old_createRandoList(41, blocklength = 4, n.block_permute = 1)$pat_id) > 0 } seed <- Filter(has_dup, 1:50)[1] seed #> [1] 1  set.seed(seed) old <- old_createRandoList(41, blocklength = 4, n.block_permute = 1) new <- createRandoList(41, blocklength = 4, n.block_permute = 1, seed = seed) attr(new, "rando_info") <- NULL   # drop the generation record for the comparison  tail(old[, c("pat_id", "block_number", "permute.block", "arm", "RanNo")], 3) #>    pat_id block_number permute.block arm  RanNo #> 39     37           10            10   B 001-37 #> 40     40           10            10   A 001-40 #> 41     32           11            11   B 001-32 old$pat_id[duplicated(old$pat_id)]                            # used twice #> [1] "32" setdiff(formatC(1:41, flag = "0", width = 2), old$pat_id)    # never used #> [1] "41" tail(new[, c("pat_id", "block_number", "permute.block", "arm", "RanNo")], 3) #>    pat_id block_number permute.block arm  RanNo #> 39     37           10            10   B 001-37 #> 40     40           10            10   A 001-40 #> 41     41           11            11   B 001-41 anyDuplicated(new$pat_id) #> [1] 0 identical(new[-41, ], old[-41, ]) #> [1] TRUE

what: How often does this happen with the SOP design?
title: Where the legacy code goes wrong, and how randolist fixes it
text: SOP block lengths (4 6, probabilities 0.75 0.25) length last block random, whether bug strikes depends seed. 300 seeds list 100 patients: Legacy code: lists per n.block_permute (rows), 300 seeds New code: lists per n.block_permute (rows), 300 seeds
code: outcome <- function(f, seed, ...) {   set.seed(seed)   res <- tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e) e)   if (inherits(res, "error")) return("stops with error")   if (anyDuplicated(res$pat_id)) return("duplicated IDs")   if (!setequal(res$pat_id, formatC(1:100, flag = "0", width = 3))) return("wrong IDs")   "correct" }  grid <- expand.grid(n.block_permute = c(1, 2, 3), seed = 1:300) grid$legacy <- mapply(function(nb, s)   outcome(old_createRandoList, s, nPat = 100, blocklength = c(4, 6),           blocklength_prob = c(0.75, 0.25), n.block_permute = nb),   grid$n.block_permute, grid$seed) grid$new <- mapply(function(nb, s)   outcome(createRandoList, s, nPat = 100, blocklength = c(4, 6),           blocklength_prob = c(0.75, 0.25), n.block_permute = nb),   grid$n.block_permute, grid$seed)  knitr::kable(table(grid$n.block_permute, grid$legacy),              caption = "Legacy code: lists per n.block_permute (rows), out of 300 seeds") knitr::kable(table(grid$n.block_permute, grid$new),              caption = "New code: lists per n.block_permute (rows), out of 300 seeds")

what: 6. No seed: the legacy list cannot be reproduced
title: Where the legacy code goes wrong, and how randolist fixes it
text: seed set session, R starts clock. legacy code runs without complaint, list exists can never made : new code stops instead (takes seed directly seed =):
code: fresh <- function() if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))   rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())  fresh(); a <- old_createRandoList(40) Sys.sleep(0.2) fresh(); b <- old_createRandoList(40) identical(a$arm, b$arm) #> [1] FALSE fresh() createRandoList(40) #> Error: #> ! No random seed has been set. Supply `seed` or call set.seed() first, otherwise the list cannot be reproduced.

title: Create a (stratified) permuted block randomisation list — createRandoList
text: nPat Number patients per stratum: single number used every stratum, one number per stratum. SOP asks least twice maximum anticipated stratum size. Strata 0 patients return NULL. arms Number arms (least 2). arm_names Arm labels, one per arm. dummy list use dummy_arm_names. NULL, arms called Arm1, Arm2, ... strata Named vector strata: names stratum names, values stratum codes used randomisation number. See composite_strata. blocklength Possible block lengths; must multiple arms. blocklength_prob Probability block length. default (equal probabilities) kept compatibility legacy function; SOP default c(0.75, 0.25), pass explicitly. first_patid Patient number first patient stratum. patid_format List formatC arguments used format patient numbers, NULL keep unformatted. n.block_permute Permute patient numbers within every n.block_permute consecutive blocks; 0 (default) means permutation Inf one permutation whole stratum. See Details. RanNo_pattern Pattern randomisation number using columns output braces, e.g. "\{stratum\}-\{pat_id\}". NULL none. seed Optional seed. given, generator set set.seed(seed, kind = "Mersenne-Twister", normal.kind = "Inversion", sample.kind = sample_kind), gives list calling set.seed(seed) function. NULL, seed must already set. sample_kind "Rounding" (default, legacy function R < 3.6.0) "Rejection" (R's current default). reproducible; use value dummy final list. seed_per_stratum TRUE, stratum generated seed seed + - 1, changing size one stratum change others. Requires seed. Lists differ legacy function mode.
